name: Tianeptine

binding.tissue_or_cell: HEK293 cells stably expressing human MOR
HEK293 cells stably expressing human DOR

biased_agonism.interpretation: Tianeptine is widely reported as a MOR full agonist with reduced β-arrestin recruitment relative to DAMGO, but quantitative bias factors are sparse in the primary literature. Behavioral tolerance/dependence develops despite the proposed bias, indicating clinically meaningful arrestin signaling remains.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Tianeptine activates canonical MOR Gαi/o coupling — inhibition of adenylyl cyclase (reduced cAMP), activation of GIRK channels, inhibition of voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels. Chronic dosing produces classical MOR tolerance with reduced analgesic and locomotor responses, mediated by receptor desensitization and downregulation in mice (Frontiers Psychiatry 2023, doi:10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1186397). Downstream BDNF/TrkB upregulation in the hippocampus appears MOR-dependent (Translational Psychiatry 2017, doi:10.1038/npp.2017.60).

neuroimaging.finding: Tianeptine induces opioid-receptor-dependent β oscillations in the rat hippocampus — naloxone-reversible.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Contraindicated — risk of hypertensive crisis and opioid potentiation

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: additive CNS depression + altered tianeptine absorption
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Reduced peak tianeptine plasma levels and enhanced sedation

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: OPRM1 A118G (N40D) carriers have altered MOR signaling and altered response to opioid agonists generally; tianeptine response data per-genotype is not established but theoretically relevant given the MOR mechanism.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Chronic tianeptine produces analgesic and locomotor tolerance in mice consistent with classical MOR downregulation/desensitization within 7-14 days of repeated dosing; cross-tolerance to morphine demonstrated.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Classical opioid withdrawal — onset 6-24 h after last dose, peak 24-72 h, lasting 5-10+ days. Symptoms: anxiety, dysphoria, sweating, GI distress, myalgia, insomnia, mydriasis, rhinorrhea, piloerection. Reported clinically indistinguishable from short-acting opioid withdrawal at supratherapeutic doses (gas-station 'Zaza' / 'Tianna' cases).

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Historical 'serotonin reuptake enhancer' (SSRE) framing is unsupported by contemporary radioligand studies; tianeptine does not meaningfully alter SERT activity in humans at therapeutic concentrations. The antidepressant effect is MOR-mediated.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: t½ extended to 4-9 h; dose reduction recommended.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal impairment prolongs elimination since tianeptine and metabolites undergo renal excretion.

data_gaps_remaining: quantitative bias factor for G-protein vs β-arrestin at MOR
human PET MOR occupancy at therapeutic dose

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Identical to tianeptine free acid in vivo — the sodium salt dissociates upon dissolution and is the form used in most clinical formulations (Stablon, Coaxil).

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Classical opioid withdrawal at supratherapeutic doses. See tianeptine entry.

name: Bromantane

primary_targets: aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC, genomic upregulation)

functional.readout: qPCR + Western blot in striatum, hypothalamus, VTA

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Genomic mechanism — bromantane elevates CREB phosphorylation, disinhibiting TH transcription that is normally suppressed by dopamine autoregulation. Effect is slow-onset (hours) and long-lasting (weeks of chronic use) compared to classical psychostimulants. σ1 receptor involvement is inferred from amantadine/memantine analogy but not directly demonstrated for bromantane.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Bromantane is uniquely described as resistant to classical stimulant tolerance — repeated dosing maintains efficacy over weeks in Russian clinical trials. Rationale: the mechanism does not deplete catecholamine stores or chronically over-stimulate post-synaptic dopamine receptors.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: No documented opioid- or amphetamine-type withdrawal in published Russian trials; possible rebound fatigue.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Inferred from amantadine analogy; not directly measured for bromantane.

data_gaps_remaining: controlled long-term safety data outside Russian Federation

name: Methylene blue

primary_targets: mitochondrial complex IV / cytochrome c oxidase (alternate electron carrier)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Biphasic mitochondrial effects: low doses enhance ATP synthesis via Complex IV electron shunting and induce mitochondrial biogenesis via PGC-1α; high doses uncouple respiration. Inhibits soluble guanylate cyclase (basis for use in refractory vasodilatory shock) and methemoglobin reductase activity (FDA-approved for methemoglobinemia). MAO-A inhibition is potent enough at therapeutic doses to cause clinically dangerous serotonin syndrome.

neuroimaging.finding: Low-dose MB (0.5-4 mg/kg PO) in healthy humans increases task-related BOLD activity in cortex and hippocampus; correlates with improved short-term memory.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Serotonin syndrome — FDA black-box-equivalent warning. Multiple deaths reported.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: G6PD-deficient patients can develop hemolytic anemia or paradoxical methemoglobinemia from MB administration — relevant for parenteral/high-dose use.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: no formal tolerance described; MAO-A inhibition is reversible.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Used therapeutically for vasoplegia (vasodilatory shock); at high doses can cause hypertension.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: biliary + urinary excretion of metabolites; renal impairment may prolong t½.

data_gaps_remaining: concentration-effect curve for cognitive enhancement in humans

name: Semax

primary_targets: BDNF/NGF upregulation in hippocampus and cortex
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Semax is rapidly cleaved (plasma t½ 2-5 min) but the active metabolite Pro-Gly-Pro (PGP) accumulates in brain and acts as a weak enkephalinase inhibitor, prolonging endogenous enkephalin signaling and BDNF transcription. Sustained behavioral effects (12-24 h) outlast the parent peptide.

data_gaps_remaining: independent Western validation of clinical claims

name: Selank

functional.target: GABAergic gene expression (IMR-32 cells, rat hippocampus)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Selank is a synthetic tuftsin analog (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg) with a C-terminal Pro-Gly-Pro tail for metabolic stabilization (mirrors semax). Anxiolytic action is attributed to (i) indirect modulation of GABA-A subunit expression and (ii) enkephalinase inhibition prolonging endogenous enkephalin signaling. The peptide enhances diazepam efficacy in chronic mild stress models.

data_gaps_remaining: direct binding data at any GABA-A subunit

name: Noopept

primary_targets: AMPA receptor positive modulation (via cycloprolylglycine metabolite)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Noopept is a prodrug: rapid esterase hydrolysis to the free acid, then cyclization to the endogenous dipeptide cyclo-Pro-Gly (cPG). cPG is an AMPA receptor positive modulator and TrkB activator, with documented neuroprotective and BDNF/NGF-upregulating effects. The short plasma t½ (<90 min) of parent compound contrasts with the longer functional effect, consistent with active metabolite mediation.

data_gaps_remaining: controlled human cognitive trials outside Russia
direct receptor binding at clinically relevant concentrations

name: Huperzine A

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: AChE inhibition is the dominant clinical mechanism — same target as donepezil/galantamine/rivastigmine. The much higher concentrations required for NMDA antagonism mean the 'dual-mechanism' marketing for neuroprotection is largely theoretical at oral doses.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Bradycardia, nausea, cholinergic crisis at supratherapeutic combined exposure

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Chronic AChE inhibition leads to modest mAChR downregulation similar to other AChE-Is.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Abrupt cessation may unmask cholinergic deficit (e.g., worsening cognition in AD).

off_targets.clinical_consequence: 900× selectivity for AChE means low peripheral cholinergic side-effect burden compared to less-selective AChE-Is.

data_gaps_remaining: validated human plasma PK at OTC supplement doses

name: 9-Me-BC

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Dual MAO-A inhibition + astrocytic neurotrophic upregulation. Inhibits MPTP→MPP+ conversion (mechanism for the parkinsonian-protection claims). The MAO-A potency is modest, but combined with chronic dosing and astrocytic BDNF effects this gives a unique pharmacological profile.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Theoretical serotonin syndrome / tyramine reaction at supratherapeutic doses; unlikely at typical reported nootropic doses (15-50 mg) but unstudied in humans.

data_gaps_remaining: binding affinity at non-MAO targets (5-HT2A, 5-HT2C, imidazoline)

name: BPC-157

functional.readout: endothelial tube formation, in-vivo wound healing

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mechanism is poorly defined. Sikiric group attributes effects to angiogenesis (VEGF upregulation), NO system modulation, and growth-hormone receptor effects. Notably stable in gastric juice (>24 h) — claimed oral bioavailability is plausible structurally but not formally documented in humans.

data_gaps_remaining: identified molecular target with binding data

functional.readout: calcium flux, AMPK/mTOR signaling, mitochondrial morphology
functional.cell_system: primary neurons, SAMP8 and APP/PS1 transgenic mice

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Binds mitochondrial α-F1-ATP synthase → modest reduction in ATP synthase activity → elevation of intracellular Ca²⁺ → activation of CAMKK2 → AMPK phosphorylation → mTOR inhibition. This is the same longevity pathway invoked by metformin and rapamycin.

functional.readout: BrdU incorporation, neurosphere formation, neurite outgrowth

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Unknown primary receptor; downstream effects include hippocampal volume increase in rodents and neurotrophic gene expression. Did not show classical antidepressant receptor binding (SERT/NET/DAT/5-HT receptors).

name: Galantamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Dual mechanism debated. Pereira's work claimed positive allosteric modulation of α4β2 and α7 nAChRs at the 'APL' site, but Kowal et al. 2018 (doi:10.1111/bph.14329) reported negative results in carefully controlled assays on human α4β2 and α7 nAChRs — calling the PAM mechanism into question. AChE inhibition remains the universally accepted dominant mechanism.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Increased galantamine exposure, increased cholinergic side effects

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs have ~25% higher galantamine AUC; UMs have lower exposure. Modest clinical impact since CYP2D6 contributes only ~25% of clearance.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: modest mAChR downregulation with chronic dosing
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Abrupt cessation in AD can worsen cognition (loss of cholinergic support).

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Reduce dose in moderate hepatic/renal impairment

data_gaps_remaining: definitive resolution of nAChR APL mechanism controversy

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Partial agonism at the α4β2 nAChR underlies both efficacy and side-effect profile. By occupying the receptor with sub-maximal activation, varenicline blocks the rewarding effect of inhaled nicotine while preventing acute withdrawal. The 5-HT3 partial agonism contributes to nausea (most common AE).

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Minimal — predominantly renal excretion makes pharmacogenetic variability low.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild — possible mood disturbance / vivid dreams during taper

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Nausea (~30% of patients) — most common AE.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Dose-reduce in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30); no hepatic adjustment needed.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Lower-efficacy partial agonism than varenicline → similar mechanism but slightly weaker craving relief, offset by lower nausea burden.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: no significant tolerance over standard 25-day course
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild nicotine withdrawal symptoms only during initial titration

binding.tissue_or_cell: Xenopus oocyte expressing human α4β2 (HS stoichiometry)
Xenopus oocyte expressing human α4β2 (LS stoichiometry)
Xenopus oocyte expressing human α7 (net charge)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Activates pre-synaptic α4β2/α6β2 nAChRs on VTA dopamine neurons → mesolimbic DA release → reinforcement. Rapid desensitization explains tolerance and the cycle of repeated dosing. α7 activation in hippocampus contributes to cognitive enhancement and sensory gating.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Increased clearance of caffeine, clozapine, olanzapine, theophylline in smokers

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2A6 slow metabolizers (e.g., *4, *9, *17 variants) have prolonged nicotine t½, lower smoking quantity, and reduced cessation success on nicotine replacement. Common in East Asian populations.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: nAChR UPREGULATION (not down) with chronic exposure — opposite of most agonist classes. Reverses over weeks of abstinence.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Onset 4-24 h, peak 2-3 days, duration 2-4 weeks. Irritability, anxiety, dysphoria, concentration impairment, increased appetite, cravings.

demographic_differences.sex: Women clear nicotine ~10-15% faster than men; estrogen induces CYP2A6. Oral contraceptives further increase clearance.

name: Alpha-GPC

primary_targets: choline / acetylcholine precursor (no direct receptor target)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hydrolyzed in gut/liver to free choline + glycerophosphate. Choline crosses BBB via CHT1 transporter and serves as substrate for ACh synthesis (rate-limited by choline acetyltransferase). Also incorporated into membrane phosphatidylcholine via Kennedy pathway. Alpha-GPC provides choline at higher BBB efficiency per mg than choline bitartrate.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Theoretical reduction of anticholinergic effect; not clinically significant at supplement doses.

data_gaps_remaining: long-term safety with chronic high doses

name: Citicoline

primary_targets: choline + cytidine donor for Kennedy pathway phosphatidylcholine synthesis
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hydrolyzed in gut to cytidine + choline; both cross BBB independently. Brain reassembles into CDP-choline → phosphatidylcholine via Kennedy pathway. Cytidine is converted to uridine in humans (humans cannot use cytidine directly), providing UTP for membrane phospholipid synthesis.

data_gaps_remaining: controlled human cognitive endpoint data in healthy adults

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hepatic esterase hydrolysis releases DMAE (deanol) and p-chlorophenoxyacetic acid (pCPA). DMAE → choline → acetylcholine in CNS. pCPA itself crosses BBB and may have direct effects (this is the pharmacological rationale for the ester being more effective than DMAE alone).

primary_targets: multiple — porcine brain hydrolysate of peptides <10 kDa
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides (15%) and free amino acids (85%) prepared by enzymatic hydrolysis of pig brain. Claimed to mimic endogenous neurotrophic factors (NGF, BDNF, CNTF, GDNF). Specific active components have not been definitively identified.

primary_targets: mitochondrial complex III (electron donor, bypassing complex I)

functional.target: Complex III of electron transport chain
functional.readout: oxygen consumption restoration in Complex-I-inhibited mitochondria

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Tissues with high NQO1 (RPE, hepatocytes) benefit most; neurons have low NQO1 expression which may limit CNS efficacy. EU approval for LHON (Raxone, 900 mg/day) and conditional approval for Friedreich's ataxia historically (withdrawn).

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: NQO1 polymorphism (C609T, *2 allele) reduces enzyme activity → reduced idebenone reduction → reduced efficacy in tissues dependent on cytosolic reduction.

name: Methylliberine

primary_targets: adenosine receptors (A1, A2A — negative allosteric / antagonist)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Caffeine-like adenosine receptor antagonist / negative allosteric modulator. Endogenous metabolic intermediate between theacrine and liberine in plant purine catabolism. Reported to slow caffeine metabolism (extending caffeine t½) when co-administered, while caffeine does not alter methylliberine PK.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Methylliberine prolongs caffeine half-life; caffeine does not alter methylliberine PK.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: adenosine receptor upregulation similar to caffeine plausible but unstudied

data_gaps_remaining: receptor binding Ki at A1, A2A

primary_targets: NMDA receptor (weak antagonist at polyamine site)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Endogenous polyamine derivative. Activity at multiple targets (imidazoline > α2 > NMDA) is generally weak. Most claimed effects (antinociception, anxiolysis) are mediated at supraphysiological doses.

name: Vinpocetine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Multi-target — PDE1 inhibition raises cAMP/cGMP (cerebral vasodilation); Na+ channel block (anticonvulsant / neuroprotective); IKK inhibition (anti-inflammatory). Plasma concentrations achievable from oral dosing fall well below the IC50s for all three targets, raising mechanistic questions about clinical efficacy.

data_gaps_remaining: mechanism reconciling in-vivo concentrations with in-vitro IC50s

primary_targets: dopamine D1 receptor density (chronic upregulation in PFC)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Lipophilic thiamine prodrug — two thiamine molecules linked by a disulfide bridge, esterified with isobutyrate. Crosses BBB more efficiently than thiamine hydrochloride. After reduction to thiamine in CNS, supports TPP-dependent metabolism (pyruvate dehydrogenase, α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, transketolase). Chronic dosing upregulates dopamine D1 receptor density in PFC in rats.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Tolerance to mood/energy effects develops over weeks; some users report dependence-like patterns and dysphoric withdrawal — atypical for a 'vitamin'.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Anecdotal reports of depressive rebound on cessation after chronic use

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Methylated resveratrol analog. Two methoxy groups dramatically improve oral bioavailability and BBB penetration. Activates AMPK and SIRT1 indirectly (likely via mitochondrial signaling rather than direct enzyme binding). Activates PPAR-α (lipid lowering) which resveratrol does not.

name: Pyritinol

primary_targets: ACh / GABA / NMDA modulation (described, not quantified)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Two vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) molecules joined by disulfide bridge — vitamin-derived semisynthetic. Crosses BBB; enhances glucose uptake/utilization in brain. Cleavage products include pyridoxal/pyridoxine (active B6 forms).

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Hepatotoxicity and cutaneous reactions (pemphigus, lichenoid) reported — particularly in elderly. Withdrawn or restricted in several markets for this reason.

data_gaps_remaining: binding affinities at claimed neurotransmitter targets

functional.readout: Nrf2 nuclear translocation, ARE-driven gene expression (NQO1, HO-1, GCL)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Master mechanism: Keap1 thiol modification → Nrf2 stabilization → ARE-driven phase II detoxification (NQO1, GST, UGT, HO-1, GCL) → antioxidant + anti-inflammatory + anti-carcinogenic effects.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: GST null genotypes have altered SFN excretion kinetics; potentially altered efficacy in chemoprevention studies.

name: Dihexa

primary_targets: HGF (hepatocyte growth factor) — augments HGF/c-Met signaling

functional.readout: c-Met phosphorylation, dendritic spine density, hippocampal synaptogenesis

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Synthetic hexapeptide derived from angiotensin IV. Binds HGF (does NOT bind c-Met directly) and stabilizes the active HGF dimer → enhanced c-Met phosphorylation → MAPK/PI3K-Akt → spinogenesis. BBB-permeable due to N-hexanoyl modification.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Theoretical oncogenic risk — HGF/c-Met signaling drives many cancers (hepatocellular, gastric, lung). Chronic supraphysiological activation is plausibly procarcinogenic. NO long-term human safety data.

data_gaps_remaining: any human PK or safety data

name: P21

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Tetrapeptide (Ac-DGGL-NH2) derived from active region of CNTF. Inhibits LIF (which normally suppresses neurogenesis) → enables hippocampal dentate gyrus neurogenesis and BDNF expression.

data_gaps_remaining: all human data — PK, safety, efficacy

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Herbal mixture; active components are oleanane-type pentacyclic triterpenoid saponins (tenuigenin, polygalasaponins XXXII, tenuifolin, onjisaponin B). Multimodal anti-AD effects in rodent models.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Nausea, vomiting at high doses (saponin emetic effect — historically used as an expectorant for this reason).

primary_targets: unknown — no formal receptor target identified
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mechanism unidentified despite 1970s development. Hansl (1978) proposed cholinergic and dopaminergic potentiation but provided no binding data. No follow-up mechanistic studies in 47 years.
α7 nAChR activation → Ca²⁺ influx → CREB → BDNF + cognitive enhancement (theorized). Failed to translate in late-stage trials.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: α7 desensitization characterized but receptor recycles rapidly

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Phase 3 in Alzheimer disease was halted in 2015 due to rare but severe GI AEs (gut motility, intussusception in animal toxicology); cognitive impairment in schizophrenia Phase 3 failed primary endpoint.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same target hypothesis as encenicline.
Abbott isoxazole nicotinic agonist analog of nicotine. Studied for AD and ADHD in 1990s-2000s; minor cognitive effects in trials, development discontinued.
Brain-selective α4β2 partial agonist designed for cognitive enhancement without peripheral ganglionic AEs. Improved attention/episodic memory in Phase 2 AAMI and ADHD trials.
Dual α7 partial agonist / 5-HT3 antagonist. Failed primary cognitive endpoint in schizophrenia Phase 2 (MCCB).

class_name: Other nootropics — kitchen-sink class with radically different mechanisms
shared_mechanism: This is NOT a true mechanistic class. The 'nootropic' label groups together compounds with completely different primary pharmacology: (1) cholinergic enhancers — AChE inhibitors (huperzine A, galantamine), choline donors (alpha-GPC, citicoline, centrophenoxine, pyritinol), and nicotinic ligands (nicotine, varenicline, cytisine, encenicline, ABT-126, ABT-418, ispronicline, RG3487); (2) atypical neurotrophic / signaling peptides (semax, selank, cerebrolysin, BPC-157, dihexa, P21); (3) glutamate / AMPA modulators (noopept→cPG, NSI-189); (4) mitochondrial agents (methylene blue, idebenone, J-147); (5) atypical psychostimulants (bromantane via TH upregulation, sulbutiamine via D1 receptor upregulation, methylliberine via adenosine antagonism); (6) Nrf2/sirtuin/longevity (sulforaphane, pterostilbene); (7) misclassified opioids — TIANEPTINE is a μ-opioid receptor full agonist with high abuse liability whose historical 'SSRE atypical antidepressant' framing is medically obsolete and dangerously underplays the true pharmacology; (8) miscellaneous (agmatine, vinpocetine, PRL-8-53, Polygala tenuifolia, 9-Me-BC).
shared_pk_summary: PK is heterogeneous: peptides (semax, selank, BPC-157) are essentially restricted to parenteral or intranasal routes due to GI proteolysis; small molecules have variable oral bioavailability ranging from very poor (~6-7% — idebenone, vinpocetine) to excellent (~80-99% — pterostilbene, tianeptine, citicoline). Half-lives range from minutes (semax parent peptide) to ~60 h (encenicline). CYP involvement is mostly limited to varenicline (minimal), galantamine (CYP2D6/3A4), and vinpocetine (CYP3A4/2C19) — tianeptine is notable for being almost entirely non-CYP cleared (mitochondrial β-oxidation).
shared_safety: Multi-target safety considerations rather than class-shared: (a) SEROTONIN SYNDROME risk with MAO-A inhibitors (methylene blue is potent enough at therapeutic doses to be a major clinical hazard with SSRIs/SNRIs/tramadol; 9-Me-BC theoretically); (b) OPIOID-RELATED HARM with tianeptine — full MOR agonism with abuse liability, withdrawal, and respiratory depression at supratherapeutic doses (this is the SINGLE most important safety message for this group); (c) CHOLINERGIC AEs with AChE inhibitors and nAChR ligands (nausea, bradycardia, GI cramping); (d) HEPATOTOXICITY reported for pyritinol; (e) PREGNANCY contraindication for vinpocetine (miscarriage risk); (f) THEORETICAL ONCOGENICITY for dihexa (chronic HGF/c-Met augmentation); (g) NO HUMAN SAFETY DATA at all for J-147, P21, BPC-157 (oral), dihexa.
sar_summary: No single SAR axis. Within sub-groups: (i) nAChR ligands — selectivity for α4β2 vs α7 vs α6β2 is structural (e.g., epibatidine/varenicline/cytisine share the pyridine-bicycle scaffold; encenicline/ABT-126 are α7-selective quinuclidine-based); (ii) peptide nootropics with C-terminal Pro-Gly-Pro tail (semax, selank) gain metabolic stability and acquire enkephalinase-inhibitor activity via the PGP metabolite; (iii) pterostilbene's two methoxy groups versus resveratrol's free hydroxyls dramatically improve oral BA and BBB penetration; (iv) tianeptine's MOR efficacy is sensitive to the heptanoate side chain length — shorter chain analogs lose efficacy.

metabolism.notes: N3-demethylation, the dominant primary pathway. Lelo 1986 measured the fractional conversion of caffeine to paraxanthine at 79.6 +/- 21.0% of dose, and 83.9% of the demethylations alone; the partial clearance to paraxanthine ran ~8x that to theobromine and ~23x that to theophylline. Jeppesen 1996 (pmid:8807660) attributes the N3-demethylation to CYP1A2: inhibiting it with fluvoxamine cut caffeine's total clearance from 107 to 21 mL/min and stretched its half-life from 5 to 31 h. Half-life 3.1 h from pmid:3756065.
N1-demethylation. 10.8 +/- 2.4% of dose, 12.1% of the demethylations. Half-life 7.2 h from pmid:3756065 — longer than caffeine's own 4.1 h.
N7-demethylation, the smallest of the three primary pathways: 3.7 +/- 1.3% of dose, 4.0% of the demethylations. Half-life 6.2 h from pmid:3756065.
Secondary pathway, downstream of paraxanthine. Its urinary excretion tracks the polymorphic N-acetyltransferase, which is why caffeine is used to phenotype NAT2.
Secondary pathway. The urinary 1-methyluric acid to 1-methylxanthine ratio is the standard xanthine-oxidase activity readout.
